The recurring trigger

The same SKU. Two plausible interpretations.

A description in your tariff master may not explain why a code was chosen. A recurring SKU deserves a record of the reasoning—and the facts that might change it.

Required inputs

  • Product description, composition, and function
  • Technical drawings and specifications
  • Relevant historical entry evidence

Prepared output

  • Two provisional rationales, kept side by side
  • Versioned product facts and explanatory references
  • Open questions and a human decision log

A specific review sequence

Make each step inspectable.

01

Link the product facts

Connect composition, construction, and intended use to their source versions.

02

Compare the competing reasoning

Make unsupported assumptions visible in both alternatives.

03

Record the reviewer’s position

Preserve rejected reasoning and the question that remains open.

01 / Inside the proposed module

A changed fact should reopen the question.

An edited assumption creates a proposed revision. The original interpretation stays in the history, and any affected review becomes outdated.

Inspect the synthetic example

02 / Inside the proposed module

Missing detail has a place in the dossier.

For HX-42, the full assembly function still needs confirmation. Neither provisional HTS candidate is assigned a legal code in this preview.

Inspect the synthetic example

03 / Inside the proposed module

Give the reviewer a concrete question.

Ask whether the imported good should be assessed by its component construction or as the complete assembly presented. The broker’s reasoning belongs alongside the evidence.

Controls & scope

What the output
can—and cannot—settle.

Suggested classifications are nonbinding. A broker or counsel must assess actual code candidates and the detailed product facts. SKUDocket does not make a government determination.

Expected reviewer: importer compliance owner and customs broker; counsel where the question requires it.

Review the limits

The pilot question

Would this help the
broker prepare the entry?

Whether the broker can use the comparison in entry preparation; material disagreements and classification rework per SKU.

Discuss offer 1

Before the next step

Questions for this offer.

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Is a suggested code binding?

No. This concept organizes competing rationales. Binding treatment requires the appropriate customs process; neither a software suggestion nor a historical entry settles the question.

Why are the demo codes unassigned?

The fictional assembly has not been broker-validated. The preview deliberately shows the reasoning without inventing authoritative-looking HTS numbers.
